text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "SchNet first computes the interatomic distance dij = ∥ri − rj∥, which makes the filter rotationally invariant [W2726670313#009]. It then expands this distance with radial basis functions ek(ri − rj) = exp(−γ∥dij − μk∥²), with centers 0 Å ≤ μk ≤ 30 Å every 0.1 Å and γ = 10 Å. The expansion adds non-linearity, so the initial filters are less correlated and training is faster [W2726670313#009]. The expanded distances are fed into two dense layers with softplus activations to compute the filter weight W(ri − rj) [W2726670313#009]."}
